correctness.rationale: The proper Boolean poset has order complex the barycentric subdivision of a simplex boundary; deleting one poset element deletes one vertex and leaves its antistar, a PL ball, so every puncture is weakly contractible by McCord. For an atom or coatom, the displayed monotone retraction respectively deletes or adjoins the distinguished element and retracts onto a subposet with a maximum or minimum. For internal ranks, every point retains either no strict upper/lower set at an extreme rank or at least two incomparable immediate upper/lower neighbors after one deletion, so there are no beat points. The non-singleton space is therefore already a Stong core and cannot be contractible. The finite verifier checks representative ranks through \(k=8\) only as corroboration.
residual_risks: The weak-contractibility proof uses the standard PL fact that the antistar of a vertex in a combinatorial sphere is a ball.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a clean complete classification in a canonical infinite family and produces, at every internal rank, explicit beat-point-free finite models that are weakly contractible but noncontractible. It sharply illustrates the gap between order-complex homotopy and finite-space contractibility, a central structural phenomenon in finite topology.
residual_risks: The family is not claimed cardinality-minimal among all such finite spaces.
